getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.html:
TCI ERP is the trade credit insurance system: the company registry, credit underwriting of buyers, policies and their terms, turnover declarations, premium, overdue notifications and claims. This section is for everyone on staff: how to sign in, how the screen is laid out, how workspaces and the acting role work, where to search and how to read your Agenda.

Start with Signing in, password and second factor, then open your role's section.

start-sign-in.title: Signing in, password and second factor
start-sign-in.html:
When to use it

On your first sign-in, after the administrator resets your password, and whenever the system asks for a second-factor code.

Steps

  1. Open the system's address, enter your email and password, then press Sign in.
  1. The first sign-in uses the temporary password the administrator gave you. The system opens the change-password page straight away: choose your own password — at least 12 characters — and save it. Until the password is changed, no other screen opens.
  2. If Two-factor authentication is on for your role, enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app. You connect the app on My account (the user menu, top right).
  3. After you sign in, the system may tell you about failed sign-in attempts with your email. If it was you, press This was me; if not, change your password and tell the administrator.

Result

The dashboard opens in your role's workspace. My account holds your password, second factor, your sessions and the display settings.

Common mistakes

  • The password is refused several times in a row. After a few failed attempts sign-in is paused, and the pause grows with each new failure. Wait for the countdown on the sign-in page to end.
  • "Forgot your password?" The administrator resets passwords: you receive a temporary password and change it when you sign in.
  • No second-factor code. Without the authenticator app you cannot sign in — contact the administrator.

start-layout.title: The screen: menu, top bar, dashboard
start-layout.html:
The menu on the left

The menu is grouped by workspace. At the top is the workspace switcher, below it "Shared" (Dashboard, Agenda, Companies, Sanctions, Help), and below that your workspace's own tools. Pin or hide the menu with the button in the top left corner or with Ctrl/⌘ + B. A hidden menu appears when you rest the pointer at the left edge of the window.

The top bar

On the left, the name of the open section. In the middle, the one search field (see Search: the one field and Ctrl/⌘ K). On the right, the «?» button (help for the open page; F1 does the same), the RU / EN / UZ language switcher and the user menu: the acting role, display settings, My account and sign-out.

The dashboard

The dashboard shows work, not a showcase: a strip of key figures (each leads to its screen), your Agenda tasks — the most urgent first — and the signals that are not zero right now.

Next to the title of almost every page there is a small «?» — it opens the help topic about that very page.

start-workspaces.title: Workspaces and the acting role
start-workspaces.html:
A person may hold several roles — say, credit analyst and credit underwriter. But they work in one role at a time: this is the acting role, and every rule in the database answers for it. Roles do not add up.

How to switch roles

  1. Open the Workspace switcher at the top of the menu.
  2. Pick a workspace: Commercial underwriting, Credit underwriting, Credit analysis, Sales, Claims, Data management or Administration.
  3. The system tells the server the new role, refreshes the data and opens the workspace's first tool.

The acting role is shown in the user menu, top right. The choice is remembered in the browser and offered at your next sign-in.

What changes with the role

  • Menu and screens — only what this role opens.
  • Agenda — the tasks of this role's department and the tasks addressed to you personally as a member of that department.
  • Buttons — for example, a credit decision is available only while acting as a credit underwriter.

If you open a link to a screen the acting role does not have, the system shows "no access" and offers to open it in another role you hold. It never switches the role by itself.

start-search.title: Search: the one field and Ctrl/⌘ K
start-search.html:
There is one search field — in the top bar. It searches the whole system and filters the list open on the page at the same time.

How to search

  1. Press Ctrl/⌘ + K or click the search field.
  2. Type a company name, a policy, claim or submission number, a registration number or a country.
  3. Separate several terms with commas — they apply in order, each narrowing what the previous left: "Samarkand, TCI-2026, UZ".
  4. Pick a result from the list, or press Enter to filter the open page.

Rules

  • A term that exactly equals a value (a policy number, a registration number) finds exactly that: "TCI-10000" does not find TCI-100001.
  • Case, accents, extra spaces and the different apostrophes of Uzbek Latin do not matter.
  • The query is kept in the page address — send a filtered list to a colleague as a link.
  • The Ctrl/⌘ + K palette also offers the acting role's actions, for example Request a company (Data management).

Company not found? Ask for it to be registered: Request it — the request goes to an information manager (see Requests for companies and statements).

start-agenda.title: The Agenda: your tasks
start-agenda.html:
My agenda is the work queue. The system creates the tasks: when a submission moves to your department, when a limit review falls due, when a policyholder files a declaration. When the work is done — the decision recorded, the rating confirmed — the task closes by itself.

Two views

  • List — one row per piece of work, grouped by due date, company or type; task-family chips with counts.
  • Triage — the queue on the left, the selected task on the right: facts, comments, history. The main button takes you to the screen where the task is done (for example, the limit decision form).

What you can do with a task

  • Snooze — the task hides until the chosen moment and comes back by itself.
  • Hand to a colleague — one task or many go to an active colleague of the same department, with an optional note. Limit validation steps and rating proposals are never handed on: who answers them is decided by authority.
  • Comment — stays in the task's history for good.

Keys: J/K — down/up, Enter or O — open, S — snooze, C — comment.

A task can almost never be closed "by hand": it closes when its reason goes away. The "Done" button exists only on notices after which nothing happens automatically.

start-companies.title: Companies and the company card
start-companies.html:
Companies is one registry: buyers and policyholders are both companies. A company's role is not assigned but computed: whoever holds a policy is a policyholder, whoever a limit is requested on is a buyer.

The company card

At the top: the name, the grade, the sanctions mark and the policyholder tier. Below, the tabs:

  • Overview — the online risk report;
  • Financials — financial statements and analysis;
  • Rating & limit — the grade, the recommended limit, rating proposals, agency ratings, ADT;
  • Limits, Policies & portfolio, Submissions, Claims;
  • Group — the corporate group, the group rating, possible relationships;
  • Sanctions — beneficial owners and screening results.

A tab shows only when it means something for this company and your role.

A new company

On entry the system checks for duplicates: the same registration number in the same country blocks creation, similar names are shown as a hint. If you may not create companies, use Request it.

start-sanctions.title: Sanctions: checking a name
start-sanctions.html:
Sanctions is open to everyone on staff. Here you check any name against the official sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, UN, EU, UK and any other loaded), see the possible matches, the loaded lists and the live sanctions flags.

Check a name

  1. Open Sanctions.
  2. Type a person's or a company's name.
  3. The system shows the nearest list entries with a similarity score. Case, Cyrillic or Latin script and the legal form ("LLC", "MChJ") do not matter.

Companies and their beneficial owners are screened automatically — when a company is added to the registry, a rating is created, a limit request is submitted, owners or the name change; and every company in the registry is screened again after a new list is loaded. A credit analyst reviews the matches (see Sanctions screening: reviewing matches).

A sanctions flag means no cover: the database refuses a new limit request, a limit approval, a submission and a policy for the flagged company or country — whoever tries.

start-display.title: Zoom, text size and colour theme
start-display.html:
Display settings are personal and kept on the server: on any computer you see the system as you set it up. They are in the user menu (Display) and on My account.

  • Zoom — 100–200 %, enlarges the whole interface, like browser zoom. The default is 150 %.
  • Text size — 100–150 %, enlarges only the text; spacing and layout stay as they are.
  • Colour theme — blue (the default), salad green, teal, plum, graphite; light, dark or "as the device".
  • Text on coloured badges — pastel badges with dark text (the default) or solid ones with white.

Printed documents — the risk report, a draft contract, a commercial offer — always print at 100 % and in the house colours, whatever you chose.

start-demo.title: Demo mode
start-demo.html:
Demo mode shows training data instead of the working data: made-up companies, policies, limits, claims and tasks. Whatever you do in demo mode stays in the demo data, and the working data is not shown meanwhile.

Switching it on and off

The Demo mode switch is in three places:

  1. the user menu, top right;
  2. the My account page;
  3. the dashboard, as the Show demo data button on the blue band.

While it is on, a yellow bar runs above every page and the top bar shows a DEMO mark. Back to real data on that bar takes you back to the working data.

Demo records are easy to spot: company names start with "DEMO", policy numbers with "DEMO-". The mode is yours alone: colleagues do not see it.

Sector grades are the exception: they are shared. The demo data is rated against the same sector grades as the working data, and a sector is reviewed with demo mode off.

Demonstration accounts

Every role has a demo account (an address ending in @demo.invalid). It always works in the demo data and cannot switch the mode off.

The administrator loads and removes the demo data: Admin › Demo data. If the lists are empty in demo mode, ask the administrator to load the demo set.

sales.title: Sales
sales.html:
Sales takes a client from the first submission to a bound policy: creates the submission, gathers the buyer package, confirms the terms, sends the client a commercial offer and, once the client agrees, binds the submission into a policy. Sales also raises credit limit requests and sees the register of active limits.

Sales does not make credit decisions and does not change policy terms — the underwriters do. A limit decision reaches the client by itself unless sales holds it before the sales window runs out; reductions and revocations reach the client at once.

sales-daily.title: A day in sales
sales-daily.html:
When to use it

Every morning and after every notice in the Agenda.

Steps

  1. Open Agenda in the Sales workspace. Typical tasks: confirm a submission's terms (due when the sales window ends), the client accepted — bind the policy, the client declined, a declaration falls due, an offer expires soon.
  2. Open Submissions: submissions in Sales confirmation are waiting for you. Check the terms and limits, prepare an offer and send it to the client (see The commercial offer).
  3. Bind submissions in Accepted into policies (see A submission: from draft to policy).
  4. An existing client needs a limit on a new buyer — Request limit (see Requesting a credit limit).
  5. Check your clients' Declarations and Overdue accounts.

Result

The Agenda is empty or holds only tasks due later.

Common mistakes

  • Waiting for the sales window to close by itself. If something is wrong with the underwriters' decision, hold it before the window ends — after that the decision goes to the client.
  • Looking for a limit decision button. Sales makes no decisions; your work is the submission and the conversation with the client.

sales-submissions.title: A submission: from draft to policy
sales-submissions.html:
When to use it

A client wants to insure trade receivables, or a client filed a submission in the portal.

Steps

  1. Submissions › New submission. Pick the policyholder or create the company, enter the expected turnover, the currency and the terms wanted.
  1. Add the buyer package: each buyer with the limit requested and the payment terms. A buyer not in the registry can be entered by name only: an information manager creates the company, and you Link it to the submission.
  2. Submit. From here it moves by itself: Entity resolution → Underwriting (credit underwriting: ratings and limits) → Commercial review (policy terms) → Sales confirmation.
  3. At Sales confirmation check the terms and the limit decisions and send the client an offer — the submission moves to With the client.
  4. The client accepts the offer in the portal (or you record their answer). The submission becomes Accepted.
  5. Bind the policy: enter the number, the inception and expiry dates. The system copies the agreed terms into the policy, adopts the package's limits onto it and moves the submission to Policy bound.

Result

A policy exists with every term and limit of the submission; the policyholder sees it in the portal.

Common mistakes

  • The client asks for other terms. The submission goes back from With the client to Sales confirmation with the client's comment in your Agenda.
  • The offer has expired. An expired offer cannot be accepted, neither in the portal nor through "My submissions"; prepare a new version.

sales-offers.title: The commercial offer
sales-offers.html:
When to use it

The submission has reached commercial review, sales confirmation or the client, and the client needs a formal offer.

Steps

  1. Open the submission and prepare an offer — in Russian, English or Uzbek. The language is chosen when the offer is prepared and does not change.
  2. Choose the parameters: the cover, the validity, whether to include the TCI brochure and a short note (up to 600 characters). The document's texts are approved and not edited; the data — terms, premium, limits per buyer, the insurer's particulars — the system fills in from the submission at every save.
  3. Check the preview on the right. A buyer's limit shows as "approved" (an effective decision), "declined" or "indicative" (the amount requested).
  4. Publish: Save and send to the client. Sales sends to the client at sales confirmation; before that the offer can be prepared, and the screen says what is missing.
  5. The client opens the offer in the portal — sales is told. The client accepts, asks for changes or declines.

Result

Accepting the offer in the portal is the client's acceptance of the submission.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting an expired offer to be accepted. The validity is binding: after it the offer cannot be accepted, only a new one requested.
  • Looking for the buyer's grade in the offer. An offer never shows a grade, the recommended limit, an authority or an internal comment.

sales-limit-requests.title: Requesting a credit limit
sales-limit-requests.html:
When to use it

An existing policyholder needs a limit on a new buyer, or a larger limit on a known one.

Steps

  1. Open the policy or Credit limits and press Request limit.
  2. Pick the buyer from the registry, enter the amount, currency, payment terms and the justification.
  3. As you type the amount, the form tells you whether it is within the policy's discretionary limit, above it and by how much.
  4. Submit. If the buyer lacks data — a registration number, an address, an industry or recent statements — the request goes to information gathering with an information manager and comes back to the queue by itself.

Result

The request is in the credit underwriting queue. You see the decision on the request page and in your Agenda.

Common mistakes

  • Raising a second request on the same buyer under the same policy. Only one request may be open per policy–buyer pair.
  • Expecting to decide it yourself. Whoever raised a request never reviews or decides it — the four-eyes rule.

commercial-terms.title: Policy terms: what each one means
commercial-terms.html:
Structure

  • Whole turnover — every buyer of the policyholder is covered (within the limits and the discretionary limit).
  • Key buyers — only the named buyers are covered.

Terms

TermWhat it means
{{term:insured-percentageInsured percentage}}The share of the loss the insurer pays, usually 80–90 %.
{{term:nqlNon-qualifying loss (NQL)}}A threshold: a loss below it is not paid at all; one equal to it is paid in full, with nothing deducted.
{{term:deductibleDeductible}}An amount taken off each loss after the insured percentage.
{{term:aflAggregate first loss}}Losses in a period the policyholder bears themselves; what is left of it is deducted.
{{term:max-liabilityMaximum liability}}The cap on all payments under the policy, usually a multiple of the premium.
{{term:dlDiscretionary limit}}Up to this amount the policyholder assesses a buyer themselves, with no limit.
Waiting periodHow many days after the overdue date a claim may be filed.
Maximum payment termsInvoices with longer terms are not covered.

The order of the indemnity

Covered debt → NQL threshold → × insured percentage → − deductible → − what is left of the aggregate first loss → no more than what is left of the maximum liability. In detail: Checking cover and calculating the indemnity.

A credit underwriter has decided and a commercial-stage task has appeared in your Agenda.

When to use it

An insurance contract must be prepared for a policy or a submission.

  • Generating the draft again over manual edits. The system asks for confirmation: the manual edits are replaced by a new version from the template.

commercial-declarations.title: Turnover declarations and premium
commercial-declarations.html:
When to use it

A policyholder has filed a turnover declaration — or premium is due.

Steps

  1. Declarations: open the filed declaration.
  2. Check the lines per buyer. The system splits the turnover: for a buyer with an active limit the whole turnover is covered; without a limit only up to the discretionary limit, and the rest is uncovered excess (not insured, and shown separately for commercial review).
  3. Accept the declaration or dispute it. On acceptance the split is frozen and premium is earned on the covered turnover at the policy's rate.
  4. The policy's premium tab: the instalment schedule, invoices, payments. A payment fills the earliest instalments first; an overpayment is refused; a mistake is corrected by a reversal, never an edit.

Result

An accepted declaration never changes; a correction is a new declaration that supersedes it.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting a refund below the minimum premium. There is no refund below the minimum premium.

When to use it

A buyer's annual or interim statements have arrived.

Steps

Result

The statements are ready for rating; if a limit request on the buyer was waiting in information gathering, it returns to the queue by itself.

  • Mixing up the units. Statements in thousands entered as units distort both the grade and the recommended limit.

analysis-rating.title: The grade: calculate, confirm, manual rating
analysis-rating.html:
When to use it

A buyer has no grade, new statements have arrived or the grade is stale.

Steps

  1. Company card › Rating & limit › calculate. The model gives the recommended grade and the recommended limit with a breakdown by factor.
  2. Confirm as is — Confirm rating. Whoever calculated a grade never confirms it.
  3. Your own grade — build the scorecard: four pillars (general, equity and debt, profit and loss, payment behaviour), each with a sub-grade, a weight and a standard reason. The system computes the weighted grade; the overall grade may differ from it only with a reason of the matching direction. A justification is required.

  4. Choose how it is approved:

    • approve myself — the grade is in force at once (if you may both rate and confirm);
    • to a colleague — a named colleague, or anyone who confirms ratings;
    • up the authority levels — escalate rank by rank up to the committee.
  5. Without statements you may propose a manual rating — with a required reason. A manual rating has no recommended limit, so no auto decision ever rests on it.

Result

The grade comes into force — and with it the rating band that sets the authority for limit decisions.

Common mistakes

  • A grade above the group rating. When the group has a rating, no member's grade may be better: the system lowers a calculated grade and refuses a proposal above it.
  • Two proposals on one buyer. Only one rating proposal per buyer may be pending.

analysis-adt.title: ADT and the group rating
analysis-adt.html:
ADT (auto decision threshold)

The ADT is the amount up to which limit requests on a buyer are decided automatically, and how many such decisions (1 to 5). It is set on the Rating & limit tab within your authority for the buyer's rating band. The counter belongs to the buyer and is shared by every policyholder.

An auto decision is made only when all conditions hold: auto decisions are switched on by the administrator, the ADT is active and not used up, the policy is active, the amount is no more than the ADT and no more than the recommended limit, and there is no stop factor (an open overdue notification, a claim, a revoked limit, a ban, stale statements, the group limit, a sanctions match, a cover-matrix restriction). Otherwise the request goes to an underwriter with the reasons listed.

A downgrade below the ADT's band, a stop factor or stale statements suspend the ADT and open the task "Buyer review / update the ADT".

The group rating

A senior credit analyst sets the group rating on the Group tab — with a reason. It caps every member's grade: setting or lowering it gives each member with a better grade a new, capped grade; raising or ending the group rating raises nobody.

credit-decide.title: Deciding a limit request
credit-decide.html:
When to use it

A limit request waits for a credit decision.

Steps

  1. Open the request: on the right, the buyer, their grade, the recommended limit, other active limits, the group, open overdue notifications.
  2. Press Start review — the request moves to Under review.
  3. Fill in the decision: Approved, Partially approved or Declined; amount, payment terms, validity, conditions. The meters above the form show your authority and the group exposure after the decision.
  4. Record decision. If the amount in UZS is above your authority for the rating band, nothing is recorded: the system offers Send for validation (see Authority, validation and the committee).
  5. If the decision would exceed the group limit, the request moves to Escalated and the credit desk gets a task.

Result

A decision never changes: a new decision supersedes the old one, and the whole history is visible. An approval goes to the commercial stage and the sales window; a decline goes at once.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting a reduction to wait for the sales window. A reduction and a revocation (Revoke limit) reach the policyholder at once.
  • Deciding without a grade. With no assessment the rating band is "unrated", and the authority for it is usually the smallest.

credit-authority.title: Authority, validation and the committee
credit-authority.html:
Authority

Authority is a matrix: person × stream (credit or commercial) × rating band (A, B, C, D, unrated) × amount × currency × validity. The request's amount is converted to UZS. Your authority is the larger of your personal grants and those of your level. Nobody's authority is unlimited, the administrator's included.

Send for validation

  1. A decision above your authority: on the request page press Send for validation. You may send one within your authority too — then a comment is required.
  2. The proposed decision goes to an authority level: in "direct" routing to the lowest rank that covers the amount (the ranks in between are told), in "sequential" routing to the next rank.
  3. While it is on validation the request is Escalated: the decision does not exist yet and the client does not see it.
  4. Any eligible member of the level answers: approve, approve modified within their own authority, return to the author, reject, or forward up.

The committee

Rank 5 is the committee. Members vote (approve, reject with a reason, abstain); a conflict of interest is declared and bars the member. Quorum is at least half; simple majority; a tie goes the chair's way; without the chair's vote the proposal returns to the author.

credit-rules.title: Four eyes, the cover matrix, information gathering
credit-rules.html:
Four eyes

  • Whoever raised a limit request never takes it into review, decides it, proposes a decision on it, validates it or adjusts it.
  • Whoever made the credit decision does not run its commercial stage.
  • In separate credit analysis, whoever calculated or confirmed the buyer's current grade does not decide the limit on it.

The cover matrix

The cover matrix raises the lowest rank that may decide, from the OECD country category (or an approved internal one) and the sector grade: categories 0–3 — no restriction, 4–5 — rank 3, 6 — rank 4, 7 and "not classified" — the committee; a D sector adds a rank. Until an OECD list is loaded, the country part is silent.

Sanctions

A sanctions flag on the buyer or its country means no cover: an approval is refused for any author. A decline, a reduction to nothing and a revocation remain possible.

Information gathering

A request whose buyer lacks a registration number, an address, an industry or statements for a period ending within 18 months goes to Gathering data. Entering the data returns it to the queue by itself; Check again checks at once. A credit underwriter may waive the requirement with a reason — never on their own request.

credit-monitoring.html:
When to use it

A limit review, a worse grade, or an overdue notification from the policyholder.

Steps

  1. Credit limits › Monitoring — what needs attention.
  2. Overdue accounts: the policyholder (in the portal) or a member of staff files the overdue notification. On filing, the limit on the buyer is suspended automatically and the policyholder sees that at once.
  3. Payment of the debt closes the notification as Paid, but does not reinstate the limit: the next limit is a fresh credit decision.
  4. If the debt is still unpaid when the waiting period ends, the notification becomes a claim.
  5. The risk has worsened — Revoke limit: a revocation reaches the policyholder at once, bypassing the commercial stage and the sales window.

Result

A revocation or a new decision is recorded as new rows of the history; earlier decisions never change.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a revocation withdraws cover for goods already shipped. Cover is judged at the shipment date, by the decision in force then.

claims-coverage.title: Checking cover and calculating the indemnity
claims-coverage.html:
Cover is judged at the shipment date

For each invoice the system reconstructs the limit in force at the shipment date from the decision history. A limit revoked today does not withdraw cover for last month's shipments, and an increase granted today does not cover them backwards.

Invoices are walked in shipment order; the debt builds up in full, covered or not — an uncovered shipment fills the limit too.

The verdict per invoice

  • A shortfall (above the limit or the discretionary limit) — part is covered.
  • A breach (payment terms beyond the maximum, a shipment outside the policy period, a revoked or declined limit, a missed notification duty) — nothing is covered.

Staff may override a verdict with a reason; the system's verdict stays beside it.

The indemnity

  1. The covered debt (after overrides).
  2. The NQL threshold: the debt is at least the threshold — otherwise nothing is payable. Equal to the threshold passes.
  3. × the insured percentage.
  4. − the deductible per loss.
  5. − what is left of the aggregate first loss after earlier claims.
  6. No more than what is left of the maximum liability.

No step goes below zero; the whole calculation is shown on the Indemnity tab.

When to use it

Steps

  1. Payments and recoveries › payment: the amount may not exceed the approved indemnity.

  • Expecting rounding to break the split. The policyholder's share is the remainder, so the two shares always add up to the amount recovered.

admin-users.title: Users and roles
admin-users.html:
When to use it

A new colleague, a change of duties, a forgotten password, a lockout.

Steps

  1. Admin › Users & roles.

  4. Users are created through the user-provisioning service. Until it is hosted, the screen says "service unavailable" and accounts are created by hand following the system owner's instructions.

Result

The user sees the workspaces of their roles.

Common mistakes

  • Giving yourself a business role to "fix" something. Business actions belong to the departments: that is what keeps the four-eyes rule.

When to use it

A new underwriter, a change in the authority structure, switching auto decisions on.

A person's authority is the larger of their personal grants and their level's. The administrator holds none.

  • A grant in a currency with no rate. Without a UZS rate such a grant is left out of the comparison.

portal-limits.title: Request, change or withdraw a limit
portal-limits.html:
When to use it

You need a limit on a new buyer, or a different limit on a known one.

Steps

  1. Credit limits › Request a limit. Find the buyer by name (at least 3 letters). Not in the list — propose them by name: the insurer registers the company.
  2. Enter the amount, currency, payment terms and the justification. The form tells you whether the amount is within the policy's discretionary limit.
  3. While underwriting has not taken the request, you can change it — Change — the amount, the terms or the justification.
  4. After that, a change is a replacement: the old request is withdrawn and a new one sent at the same time.
  5. Any open request can be withdrawn — Withdraw the request.

Result

Every change is kept and visible to the insurer.

Common mistakes

  • A second request on the same buyer. One policy may have only one open request per buyer — change the existing one.

portal-declarations.title: Declarations and premium
portal-declarations.html:
When to use it

A turnover declaration or a premium instalment is due.

Steps

  1. Declarations: enter the turnover per buyer and country for the period and file the declaration.
  2. Turnover with a buyer that has a limit is covered in full; without a limit, up to the discretionary limit; the rest is not insured.
  3. Once accepted, a declaration does not change: a correction is filed as a new declaration.
  4. Premium: the instalment schedule, the invoices and the payments received.

Result

Premium is earned on the accepted declaration.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting a refund below the minimum premium. The minimum premium is not refunded.

portal-claims.title: Overdue accounts and claims
portal-claims.html:
When to use it

A buyer has not paid an invoice on time.

Steps

  1. Overdue accounts: report the overdue account — buyer, invoices, amounts, dates. Do it within the time your policy sets: a late notification can take the cover away.
  2. After the notification the limit on this buyer is suspended — new shipments to them are not covered.
  3. If the buyer pays — report it; the limit is not reinstated automatically, a new request is needed.
  4. If the debt is still unpaid after the waiting period — Claims: file a claim with the required documents.
  5. Answer the information requests — they arrive in the portal.

Result

The claim is assessed; the decision and the payment are visible in the portal.

Common mistakes

  • Reporting an overdue account late. The notification deadline is in your policy; a late notification can take the cover away from the whole claim.

glossary-terms.title: Terms
glossary-terms.html:
Acting role

The role a person works in now; every rule answers for it. It changes when the workspace is switched.

ADT

Auto decision threshold: the amount up to which limit requests on a buyer are decided automatically, and how many such decisions (1–5). Set within authority; an auto decision only when every condition holds and there is no stop factor.

Agenda

A person's task queue. The system opens and closes the tasks from events; people work them, snooze, comment on or hand them to a colleague.

Aggregate first loss

(AFL) Losses in a period the policyholder bears themselves; what is left of it after earlier claims is deducted from the indemnity.

Annulment

The policy is treated as never concluded and the premium is returned. Not the same as cancellation.

Authority

The amount up to which a person decides alone — per stream, rating band, currency and validity. Nobody's authority is unlimited.

Authority level

Rank 1–4 with the level's grants and members; rank 5 is the committee. A proposed decision goes to a level, not to a named person.

Beneficial owner

The person who ultimately owns or controls a company; screened against the sanctions lists.

Buyer

The policyholder's debtor, whose credit risk is insured. Not our client.

Cancellation

The policy ends from a date; everything before it stands.

Claim

The policyholder's demand for an indemnity on a buyer's unpaid debt. Numbered CL-YYYY-NNNN.

Commercial offer

The document for the client with the terms, premium and limits of a submission. The texts are approved, the system fills in the data; an offer has a validity.

Committee

The highest, fifth authority rank. Decides by vote: quorum of half, simple majority, a tie goes the chair's way.

Cover matrix

The rule by which the OECD country category and the sector grade raise the lowest rank that may decide a limit.

Credit limit request

A request for a limit on a buyer under a policy or a submission. Only one may be open per policy–buyer pair; its decisions never change, a new one supersedes the old.

Deductible

An amount taken off each loss after the insured percentage.

Discretionary limit

(DL) The amount up to which the policyholder assesses a buyer themselves, without a separate credit limit.

Escalate

Send a proposal up the authority levels — rank by rank, up to the committee.

Four eyes

The rule that the author of a request does not decide it, and whoever calculated a grade does not confirm it.

Grade

The buyer's credit risk assessment in force, on the scale A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D. In force once a person confirms it.

Group limit

The cap on the total exposure to a corporate group; a decision beyond it is raised to be decided with the whole group in view.

Group rating

A grade for a corporate group; it caps every member's grade. A senior credit analyst sets it.

Information gathering

The status of a limit request whose buyer lacks data; it clears by itself once the data is entered.

Insured percentage

The share of the loss the insurer pays, usually 80–90 %.

Limit revocation

A risk action: the limit stops covering new shipments; it reaches the policyholder at once.

Manual rating

A grade a person sets with a required reason, possibly without statements. It has no recommended limit.

Maximum liability

The cap on all the insurer's payments under a policy, usually a multiple of the premium.

Non-qualifying loss (NQL)

A threshold: a loss below it is not paid at all; one equal to it or above is paid in full, with nothing deducted for the threshold.

Overdue notification

The policyholder's report that a buyer has not paid an invoice beyond the maximum payment terms. It suspends the limit on the buyer.

Policyholder

Our client — the seller who insured their receivables.

Policyholder tier

Bronze, silver, gold or platinum — by insured turnover and premium. A service class; it affects no decision.

Possible match

A company's or a person's name resembles a sanctions list entry. It waits for a credit analyst's review and blocks a limit approval until then.

Rating band

The family of a grade — A, B, C, D or "unrated". Authority for limit decisions is set per band.

Rating proposal

A grade an analyst proposed that waits for a colleague's or an authority level's approval.

Rating scorecard

Four pillars of assessment — general, equity and debt, profit and loss, payment behaviour — with sub-grades, weights and reasons, from which the system computes the weighted grade.

Recommended grade

The grade the model calculates, before a person confirms it.

Recommended limit

The limit the model calculates from the buyer's statements.

Request withdrawal

The author of a request or the client gives it up; the request closes without a decision.

Sales window

The time sales has to hold a limit decision before it reaches the client. Not held — the decision goes by itself.

Sanctions

A sanctions flag on a country or a company means no cover; the database refuses new limits, submissions and policies for it.

Submission

A client's way from enquiry to policy: entity resolution, underwriting, commercial review, sales confirmation, the client's answer, binding.

Turnover declaration

The policyholder's periodic report of insured sales per buyer and country; the basis of the premium.

I switched the language — some data stayed in another language. The interface is fully translated; company names, comments and documents stay in the language they were entered in.

Where do I see who changed a decision and when? Decisions, status history and events never change — a new one supersedes the old, and the whole chain is shown on the object's page.

An amount shows as "—". The value is unknown (for example, there is no exchange rate). An empty value is never shown as zero.

What is demo mode? Training data whose names start with DEMO; switched on in the user menu, see Demo mode.

"A new version of TCI ERP is available" appeared. The system was updated. Save what you typed and press the reload button in the notice.
